# The Unhurried Turning

## Scripture
"The path of the righteous is like the morning sun, shining ever brighter till the full light of day." — Proverbs 4:18

## Reflection
Tonight, look up and find the moon—wherever it is in its cycle. Perhaps it is a slender crescent, a glowing half, or a full silver disc. The moon doesn't rush. It takes a full month to complete its phases, and yet it never misses a single turning. It moves at God's pace, unhurried and faithful.

Our faith often feels like that moon. There are seasons when we are a sliver of what we hope to be—dim, partial, still growing. Other seasons feel full and radiant. But the moon teaches us something profound: every phase is part of a faithful rhythm, not a failure. The crescent is not less than the full moon; it is simply earlier in the turning.

God is patient with your phases. He isn't frustrated by your partial shine. The same hand that set the moon in its orbit is gently turning you toward more light—not all at once, but steadily, dependably, like a faithful witness in the night sky. Your path, like the morning sun, is shining ever brighter. It may not feel bright tonight. But the turning has already begun.

## Prayer
Father, you who hold the moon in its course, hold me in my slow growth. When I feel like a thin crescent, remind me that I am still turning toward your light. Give me patience with my own seasons, and trust in your unhurried work. Amen.
